progression.startsWith: Remember the stockroom bottle from the mass spectrometry video? Its molecular ion was at seventy-two, and four candidate structures were still in the running. That spectrum couldn't finish the job, and no single spectrum can. But now you've met infrared and both kinds of NMR. Put the evidence together, and only one structure should survive.
progression.stopsAfter: giving each technique its question; using mass with the elements present; using present and missing IR bands; counting carbon environments; matching proton areas to the formula and reading patterns; assembling a structure; ruling out a close isomer by a predicted contradiction; checking every clue; recognising corroboration.
progression.nextLesson: integrated structure practice with chemical tests and spectra (route chem-m8-g03).

teaching.task: The stockroom bottle from the mass spectrometry video still has four candidates. How do you use every spectrum together so that only one structure survives?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) one spectrum left four candidates; the right structure must fit every spectrum (1); (2) each technique answers one question; a good order (2); (3) the mass narrows the formula; the stated oxygen fixes it (3); (4) a C=O dip and a missing O–H band rule out the alcohol and leave three carbonyl isomers (4); (5) four ¹³C peaks rule out the symmetrical 2-methylpropanal; the carbonyl peak can't separate aldehyde from ketone (5); (6) proton areas match the formula's 8 H; the ethyl pattern and the lone CH₃ singlet (6); (7) the pieces join one way: butanone (7); (8) predict the close isomer's spectrum and find the contradiction (8); (9) check every clue; strongly supported (9); (10) one band decides, a second technique agrees (10); memory aid (11); attempts (12 to 15); decision rule and handoff (16); key notes (17).
teaching.conversationalApproach: Remember the stockroom bottle from the mass spectrometry video? Its molecular ion was at seventy-two, and four candidate structures were still in the running. Each technique answers a different question. Step one, the mass. Step two, the bonds. Step three, the carbon map. Step four, the hydrogens. Now build it. But could it still be butanal? Test it the other way round. Then check butanone against every clue. Sometimes one technique settles it fast. One line to keep: mass, groups, map, then check every clue. Your turn. It's 2-chloropropane. Last one. It's ethyl propanoate. So, when you're given several spectra, take them in order.
teaching.openingDecision: Remember the stockroom bottle from the mass spectrometry video? Its molecular ion was at seventy-two, and four candidate structures were still in the running. That spectrum couldn't finish the job, and no single spectrum can. But now you've met infrared and both kinds of NMR. Put the evidence together, and only one structure should survive.
teaching.understandingCheck: Your turn. This compound contains only carbon, hydrogen and chlorine. Use its mass spectrum and both NMR spectra to identify it, and justify your answer with each spectrum. Pause here to answer. Last one. Compound Z is C five H ten O two, and it's one of the four compounds on the card. Use the infrared and proton NMR data to identify it, and justify your answer. Pause here to answer.
teaching.curriculumScope:
Syllabus dotpoint (as printed; NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, p58; C8-IQ2-02 is this project's local catalogue ID, not a code printed in the syllabus), quoted from ../../programme/syllabus/chem-2017-y12.json:

"investigate the processes used to analyse the structure of simple organic compounds addressed in the course, including but not limited to:
- proton and carbon-13 NMR
- mass spectrometry
- infrared spectroscopy (ACSCH130)"

design.visualSystem: spectra are coded diagrams only, using the components the c09 to c11b designs specify (c09's stick spectrum and gap bracket; c10's IR trace, band marker, range shade, empty-range shade and data sheet card; c11a's NmrSpectrum in carbon mode with environment rings and data sheet card; c11b's proton mode with multiplets, environment brackets and the integration line), never AI images; every spectrum's values are realistic for the named compound and every drawn peak is listed under "Numbers to verify"; the bottle and the three instruments are existing painted plates listed by filename, never stretched; molecules from the coded molecule kit; no people, hands or faces; at most about three bright text items, earlier deductions kept on screen but dim; one reasoning stage at a time; "Pause here to answer." then a 10 s countdown with the full worded question and its data kept on screen; no givens card, givens underlined in the feedback as they are used; brief feedback (answer, key reason, one crossed mistake, about 15 to 30 s); original HSC-style questions only; Australian spelling; no em dashes; conversational narration; no absolute claims ("fits", "strongly supported", "rules out" only for a stated candidate that would give a contradicting signal).
design.transitionPlan: heading writes on: "Which structure fits every clue?". the instrument plates shrink to the ledger rows, one beside each label. the butanone stick spectrum fills the dock (Numbers to verify; c09 values), its 72 bar gold. butanone's IR trace draws left to right in the dock (Numbers to verify), with c10's IR data sheet card small at the upper right, only the C=O and O–H rows bright. butanone's ¹³C spectrum draws right to left in the dock (four lines near 209, 37, 29 and 8; TMS grey at 0; Numbers to verify), the lines grey at first. butanone's proton spectrum draws in the dock (quartet near 2. the right card clears. butanal enlarges from the strip, its CHO hydrogen ringed. butanone sits centre right; the four ledger rows brighten one at a time as each clue is spoken, and a thin line runs from each row to the part of butanone it explains: "MS" to the whole molecule ("72"), then the two C–C bonds beside the C=O ("43, 57": c09's two break points, grey chip "c09"); "IR" to the C=O; "¹³C" to its four carbons ringed in four colours; "¹H" to its three hydrogen sets. the board clears. the board clears. the board clears. the card stays, shrunk to the top. question card, worded as printed (A2 under Decisions): the formula, the four names as a compact list (one line each), the IR as its two printed observations (no IR trace), the four proton signals with shifts, splitting and areas, and the two printed shift notes. the card stays, shrunk to the top. the board clears. Heading on screen: "Key notes: what to write in your book".
